rules.text: A block's body (after if, for, def) must be indented 4 spaces. Python reads indentation as part of the code.
Numbers and text are different types. Turn a number into text with str() before joining with +.
Average = total divided by HOW MANY items, i.e. len(list), not a fixed number.
Watch the boundary: > means 'greater than', >= means 'greater than or equal to'.
Read the LAST line of an error first: the error type and explanation are there.
A test (assert) is a promise about how code behaves. Code is done when every test passes, edge cases included.
Change one thing, run the tests again. Guessing with many changes at once gets confusing.
APPROVE when the code is correct, readable, and its tests pass. Don't hold back good work.
REVISE when there is a bug, a missed edge case, or a risky habit. Point to the problem line.
Passwords and secret keys must never be written in code. Keep them in secret settings (environment variables).
ESCALATE to a senior developer when a change needs special permission or expertise (production servers, customer data).
